subject: Metering clarification for NovaRetail pilot: token rounding, context credits, and sample invoice
messages:
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@novaretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-15T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Metering clarification for NovaRetail pilot

Hi Hannah,

Quick question from procurement as we finalize the pilot SOW: how does Redwood meter a mixed workload where some calls are very short (user utterance + short assistant reply) and others are long-context (system prompt + 8k context + long generation)? Specifically: 

- Do partial tokens round up per-call or per-invoice line?
- If we have a long conversation that reuses KV cache across many short follow-ups within a session, do we get credit for the cached prefix or is every call billed for the full context length?
- Is there a minimum billable unit per call (e.g., floor of N tokens) or a 1-token granularity?

Procurement also asked for a sample invoice line showing 1,200 short calls (avg 18 tokens in/out) and 300 long calls (avg 6,500 tokens in/out) for a month so they can map to their PO. Can you send a one-page explanation + a worked example with numbers we can attach to the PO?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Li
Head of Platform (NovaRetail)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Metering clarification for NovaRetail pilot

Jordan — thanks for the clear examples. We're happy to provide an explicit worked example and a short explainer you can attach to the SOW. Quick, high-level answers first (details and a CSV with line-item math attached in my next email):

- Rounding: Redwood charges at token granularity (after subtokenization). Partial subtokens are rounded up per request. There is no additional billing-level rounding at invoice aggregation — we sum billable tokens across calls.
- KV cache/context reuse: By default, we bill for the tokens actually provided to the runtime per request. When a request benefits from cached KV (e.g., repeated system prompt or prefix reused within a 30-minute session), the runtime omits sending the cached KV to the accelerator and we reflect that in our metering (you will see reduced billable input tokens). We also offer an optional session-aggregation feature (30-min window) that will aggregate short calls and apply a small effective credit when key prefixes are repeatedly reused — I'll note the default behavior vs. session-aggregation in the example.
- Minimums: For the hosted API we apply a per-call micro-floor of 3 tokens to prevent abuse (rare edge case); for Dedicated / committed pilots we can set a negotiable per-call floor or roll it into a monthly minimum.

Attaching a worked CSV and the pricing sheet in a follow-up — sending that now to Ben and Vivek for any adjustments before I send to you. If procurement needs an official paragraph for the PO, tell me which legal name to use and I'll draft it.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Metering clarification for NovaRetail pilot — example math

Hannah — adding some concrete breakouts so Jordan gets a line-by-line he can paste into procurement. I kept numbers conservative and called out where pilot discounts could apply. Paste into the one-pager: 

Ruleset we used in the example (default hosted behavior unless we agree otherwise for the pilot):
- Token granularity: 1 token after subtokenization; partial subtokens rounded up per call.
- Per-call micro-floor: 3 tokens (applies when total in+out tokens < 3).
- KV cache credit: when identical prefix is reused within 30 minutes for the same session_id, we do not re-send the prefix to the runtime; billable input tokens reflect what the runtime receives.
- Session-aggregation (optional): we can enable an aggregation window (30m) that collapses repeated short calls into an effective per-call average for billing (used in some pilots to avoid microbilling noise).

Worked example (numbers to attach to PO):
1) Short calls: 1,200 calls, avg input 8 tokens, avg output 10 tokens => avg 18 tokens/call. With 1-token granularity and no floor hit, billable = 1,200 * 18 = 21,600 tokens.
2) Long calls: 300 calls, avg input 4,000 tokens, avg output 2,500 tokens => 6,500 tokens/call. If KV cache is effective and the 4,000-token prefix is cached for repeated follow-ups, we show a conservative 20% reduction to input tokens for 40% of long calls in this sample (pilot-specific). That yields:
   - Fully-billed long calls (no cache): 180 calls * 6,500 = 1,170,000 tokens
   - Cache-reduced long calls: 120 calls * (6,500 * 0.8) = 624,000 tokens
   Total long-call billable tokens = 1,794,000 tokens.

Invoice sample (pre-discount):
- Short calls: 21,600 tokens
- Long calls: 1,794,000 tokens
- Total tokens = 1,815,600 tokens

Assume list price $0.0002 / token (example price for spool):
- Gross = 1,815,600 * 0.0002 = $363.12

Pilot discount suggestion (we can make this formal): 15% off gross for the pilot month => $308.65.

Attachments: I prepared nova_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx and redwood_metering_examples.csv with the per-call lines and the math above; Hannah will send to Jordan. If procurement wants a ’how we meter’ clause, we should provide language that: (a) defines tokenization/reference implementation, (b) documents the 30m aggregation window option, and (c) states that we will provide a sample invoice for the pilot month before final PO acceptance.

— Vanessa
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference

Jordan — attaching the two files: nova_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx (three price scenarios and a sample invoice layout) and redwood_metering_examples.csv (line-level math for each call). Key points we included in the one-pager for procurement (copy/paste friendly):

"How Redwood measures billable tokens" (suggested PO language):
- Tokenization/system: Billable units are computed after standard subtokenization (Byte-Pair Encoding / model tokenizer). Partial subtokens are rounded up to the next whole token per request.
- Context and caching: Billable input tokens reflect the actual tokenized input that the Redwood runtime receives. When identical prefixes are reused within the same session_id and within a 30-minute aggregation window, Redwood omits re-sending cached KV to the runtime and reflects lower billable input tokens. The 30-minute window is configurable for Dedicated pilots; for hosted pilots the default is 30 minutes and can be extended by request (subject to operational review).
- Minimums and floors: Default per-call micro-floor = 3 tokens. For pilots with a committed monthly minimum, this micro-floor can be removed or rolled into the monthly commit.
- Invoice reconciliation: Redwood will provide a sample invoice for the pilot month within 7 business days of month-end and will reconcile any discrepancies against usage logs within 30 days.

We included the three price scenarios ($0.00015, $0.00020, $0.00025) in the pricing sheet and the CSV shows the per-call breakdown (short calls / long calls / cache adjustments). On the pilot discount, we proposed 15% in the sample invoice but can update to whatever you prefer.

If procurement is satisfied with the paragraph above, we can include it verbatim in the SOW. Next steps: if you confirm the PO language, we'll (1) enable session-aggregation for your pilot with a 30-minute default, (2) lock in the pilot discount, and (3) send a Draft Invoice preview after the first full month of usage.

Would you like me to send this to your procurement contact directly as a PDF attachment?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
